sections.title: VERSES 21-24 UNBELIEVERS WHO ASK FOR ANGELS TODAY WILL ASK FOR A STONE BARRIER BETWEEN THEM AND THE ANGELS OF PUNISHMENT

translation.text: Those who do not expect to meet Us say, “If only the angels were sent down to us, or we could see our Lord!” They have certainly been carried away by their arrogance and have entirely exceeded all limits.

commentary.text: The Stubbornness of the Disbelievers

The disbelieves attitude is one of arrogance, pride and ridicule because they have no hope or fear regarding the DoJ. They mockingly ask: Why did Allah SWT not send an angel as a messenger? Why does Allah SWT not show himself to us?

translation.text: On that Day - the Day when they will behold angels - there will be no good news for those immersed in evil, and they will cry out: "We seek refuge (in Allah)."

commentary.text: When the angles finally descend – at the time of death -- it will be a painful meeting for the disbelievers. The angels will strike them on their faces and body saying now taste the punishment. All the arrogance and pride will be gone.

translation.text: Then We will turn to whatever ˹good˺ deeds they did, reducing them to scattered dust.

commentary.text: The deeds of a disbeliever, no matter how good or noble, will be scattered like fine dust, thus, will hold no weight or value. This is because they were based on wrong beliefs that is, (i) they were not done exclusively for Allah SWT and (ii) not done according to the sunnah.

This is the third time this concept has been mentioned. First two times this concept was mentioned in the form of a parable/example in Surah Ibrahim (scattered ashes) and Surah Nur (mirage) but here there is no ambiguity or confusion re: the fate of the deeds of the disbeliever.
Note: Such people will get their reward in this world in the form of worldly praise and adoration via monuments, wings in hospitals, statues etc. but will get no recompense in the Hereafter.
Lesson: Understand the criteria for what constitutes ‘good deeds’ in Islam so that one’s entire life efforts are not scattered like fine dust.

sections.title: VERSES 25-31 DISBELIEVERS SHALL REGRET ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT NOT ADOPTING THE RIGHT PATH

arabic_lines: وَيَوۡمَ يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ عَلٰى يَدَيۡهِ يَقُوۡلُ يٰلَيۡتَنِى اتَّخَذۡتُ مَعَ الرَّسُوۡلِ سَبِيۡلًا

translation.text: On that Day the evildoer will bite his own hand and say, ‘If only I had taken the same path as the Messenger.
Woe to me! I wish I had never taken so-and-so as a close friend.

commentary.text: Regret upon regret – regret over friends that took us away from the zikr of Allah SWT, regret over peer pressure to conform, regret over not reading the Quran (the Quran will be an intercessor for us on the DoJ). On the DoJ the sky will be rip apart and angels will descend—(finally people will be able to see these angels as there will be no more barriers.)

“Day of Judgment” is also called the “Day of Regret” because people will curse themselves (bite their own hands in anger/frustration/regret) for not being able to differentiate between right path and wrong : AL-FURQAN.

Lesson: Understand the criteria for friendships. Be very aware/beware of those people/surroundings that distance you from Allah SWT by their erroneous advice, thinking etc.  And actively seek those who bring you closer to Allah SWT.

sections.title: VERSES 32-34 ALLAH EXPLAINS THE WISDOM BEHIND REVEALING AL-QURAN PIECEMEAL RATHER THAN ALL AT ONCE

translation.text: Those who disbelieve say: "Why was the Quran not revealed to him all at once?" It was revealed thus that We may fully strengthen it upon your heart/mind; (and for the same end) We have revealed it gradually (according to a scheme) in fragments.

commentary.text: The Reason why the Quran was revealed in Stages

This objection by the disbelievers of Makkah was repeated over and over again. The Quran addresses this objection at several places, see (E.Ns 101-106 of Surah An-Naml) and (E.N. 119 of Surah Bani Israil). Their question implied: “Had the Quran been really the Word of Allah SWT, it would have been sent as a complete book all at once; for Allah SWT has the knowledge of everything and every human affair”. Thus, they felt that it was obvious that nothing was being sent down from above rather the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) himself fabricates or plagiarizes all its themes from other people or other books.
The following explanation as to why the Quran was revealed piecemeal or by degrees:
So that the Prophet (PBUH) may commit it to memory perfectly and recite it to his people, who were mostly illiterate, rather than present it in a written form.
So that its teachings and messages may be imprinted deeply in the minds.
So that the way of life it teaches, may be followed with complete conviction, which would not be possible if all the commandments and the whole system of life had been sent down all at once.

So that the hearts of the Prophet and his followers may be strengthened. This required that the divine guidance and messages of encouragement should be revealed as and when needed. Obviously, this could not have been possible if these had been sent down all at once. This also shows that Allah SWT did not leave His Messenger alone amidst persecution rather that Allah SWT was watching the struggle with concern; guiding and helping His Prophet through every difficulty by direct communion at every critical situation.

translation.text: (This was also done so that) whenever they put any strange question to you, We sent its right answer and explained the matter in the best manner.

commentary.text: This is yet another point of wisdom for revealing the Quran by degrees. Allah SWT sent necessary instructions and guidance as and when needed so as to answer objections and remove doubts thus providing the correct interpretation of things, for example, after the accusation of slander is Surah Nur the commandments of hijab and entry into homes was revealed.

arabic_lines: اَلَّذِيۡنَ يُحۡشَرُوۡنَ عَلٰى وُجُوۡهِهِمۡ اِلٰى جَهَـنَّمَۙ اُولٰٓـئِكَ شَرٌّ مَّكَانًا وَّاَضَلُّ سَبِيۡلًا

translation.text: Those who shall be mustered in the Hell upon their faces, their stand is the worst and their way most erroneous.

commentary.text: Some will be hurled towards Hell upon their faces because in this life they were so high-handed and arrogant that they objected to and rejected the word of Allah SWT. So now their heads will be lowered.

Lesson: Be very careful how you talk about the Quran and how you raise objections to things that you might not fully understand or that may not make sense to you. These are divine laws and It’s a crime and serious offense to say something is unfair or object to Allah's laws.

sections.title: VERSES 35-44 ALL NATIONS WHICH REJECTED ALLAH'S REVELATIONS AND HIS RASOOLS WERE UTTERLY DESTROYED AND THOSE WHO HAVE TAKEN THEIR DESIRES AS THEIR GODS ARE NOTHING BUT ANIMALS

arabic_lines: اَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ اِلٰهَهٗ هَوٰٮهُ ؕ اَفَاَنۡتَ تَكُوۡنُ عَلَيۡهِ وَكِيۡلًا ۙ

translation.text: Have you ever considered the case of him who has taken his carnal desire for his god? Can you take responsibility for guiding him to the Right Way?

commentary.text: Those who continue to follow their desires/whims are being addressed here. Despite the dire warnings and then destruction of previous nations including Pharon, Ad and Thamud still these people do not take heed. Greed, money, addition, temptation, etc., becomes their goal or their obsession in life. Such people are completely self-absorbed and least bothered about the distinction between the right and the wrong, the true and the false -- AL-FURQAN.
Note: For a Muslim his/her sole focus in life should be Allah SWT.

“The person who makes his desire as his god” is the one who becomes the slave of his lusts and desires. According to a tradition, related by Abu Hurairah, the Prophet (PBUH) said: ‘Of all the false gods being worshipped and served instead of Allah SWT, the worst in the sight of Allah is one’s own lust.’
For further explanation, see (E.N. 50 of Surah Al-Kahf).

The Prophet said: (i) Following desires and (ii) devising lengthy plans (planning far into the future) are two things we should be cautious about as they tie us to this world and we forget the Hereafter.

arabic_lines: اَمۡ تَحۡسَبُ اَنَّ اَكۡثَرَهُمۡ يَسۡمَعُوۡنَ اَوۡ يَعۡقِلُوۡنَ ؕ اِنۡ هُمۡ اِلَّا كَالۡاَنۡعَامِ بَلۡ هُمۡ اَضَلُّ سَبِيۡلًا

translation.text: Do you think that most of them hear or understand? For they are merely like cattle; nay, even worse than them.

commentary.text: People who worship their desires or blindly follow their lusts are likened to cattle. Just as sheep and cattle do not know where their shepherd is taking them i.e. to the meadow or to the slaughter house, similarly these people are also blindly following their leaders (people or their own whims and desires) without knowing or judging whether they are being led, to success or to destruction.
It is a pity that human beings who are endowed with reason should behave like cattle, then their condition is worse than that of cattle.

Theme continues regarding the importance of beneficial associations/friendships and our strong connection to the Quran vs. living in heedlessness, ignorant to the commandments of Allah SWT. Different beliefs/behaviors result in very different outcomes. Understand the criteria between right and wrong. AL-FURQAN
Also see: (25:28) Woe to me! I wish I had never taken so-and-so as a close friend.

sections.title: VERSES 45-50 ALLAH HAS MADE THE NIGHT A MANTLE, SLEEP TO REST, AND THE DAY TO WORK

translation.text: And it is Allah Who has ordained the night as a garment for you, and the sleep as a repose of death, and the day as the time of return to life.

commentary.text: Night time is a covering so that we can rest. Sleep is a mercy. Then the day is made so that we come back to life (literally and figuratively), thus the day is for movement and getting our work done.
Note: On the DoJ we will come back to life from our graves.

sections.title: VERSES 51-60 DO NOT YIELD TO THE UNBELIEVERS; MAKE JIHAD AGAINST THEM WITH AL-QURAN AND PUT YOUR TRUST IN EVER-LIVING (ALLAH), WHO WILL NEVER DIE

arabic_lines: فَلَا تُطِعِ الۡكٰفِرِيۡنَ وَ جَاهِدۡهُمۡ بِهٖ جِهَادًا كَبِيۡرًا

translation.text: So, (O Prophet), do not follow the unbelievers but engage in a mighty striving against them with this Qur'an.

commentary.text: The Arabic words jihad-i-kabir جِهَادًا كَبِيۡرًا implies three meanings: (1) To exert the utmost effort/striving for the cause of Islam (2) To dedicate all resources to this cause. (3) To fight against the enemies of Islam on all possible fronts with all the resources in order to raise the “Word of Allah SWT”. This includes jihad of the tongue, the pen, wealth, life and every other available weapon.
The Prophet (PBUH) was offered money, power, position etc., to stop conveying the message. But Allah SWT says continue conveying the message and in fact, strive very hard.

translation.text: And He it is Who has joined the two seas: one sweet and palatable and the other saltish and bitter; and He has set a barrier and an insurmountable obstruction between the two that keeps them apart.

commentary.text: This phenomenon that sweet/fresh/delicious water and bitter/salty water exist side by side yet they do not mix due to a barrier between them. Similarly, truth and falsehood do not mix there is a barrier between the two. Surah Al-Furqan is the name of the Surah – the criteria between good and evil.

arabic_lines: وَاِذَا قِيۡلَ لَهُمُ اسۡجُدُوۡا لِلرَّحۡمٰنِ قَالُوۡا وَمَا الرَّحۡمٰنُ اَنَسۡجُدُ لِمَا تَاۡمُرُنَا وَزَادَهُمۡ نُفُوۡرًا

translation.text: When they are told: "Prostrate yourselves before the Merciful One," they say: "What is the Merciful One? Shall we prostrate ourselves before whomsoever you command us to prostrate? This even further increases their aversion.

commentary.text: (AYAT OF SAJDAH TALAWAT)
Condemnation of the Idolators
Then Allah SWT rebukes the idolators who prostrate to idols and rivals instead of Allah SWT.

When the disbelievers of Makkah are told to bow down to Allah SWT they said why should we bow down to the one whom the Prophet (PBUH) tells us? This is said due to their extreme arrogance and stubbornness. Prostration is the ultimate form of humility and submission and the last thing an arrogant person will do. They ask who is Rehman? We only know Allah. Their arrogance knows no bounds.

FYI – In the next Ayat’s we will find the complete contrast in those who truly humble themselves before Allah SWT. We will study the qualities, personality of A true Believer who is called (The slave of Rehman)     عَعِبَادُ الرَّحۡمٰنِ
In Surah Al-Mu'minun (The Believer) we learn about the qualities of a true Believer. Now we are being told about the very special characteristics and traits found in     عَعِبَادُ الرَّحۡمٰن
This is a title given by Allah SWT but only for some very special Believers. (The slave of Rehman)     عَعِبَادُ الرَّحۡمٰنِ

All scholars agree that here a prostration of recital (Sajdah Talawat) has been enjoined, which means that every reader and every hearer must prostrate himself on reciting or hearing the recital of this Ayat. According to traditions, the one who hears this Ayat being recited should say: Zadan Allahu khuduan - aenama - zada liladaai nufura: May Allah increase us in humility - even as - the enemies are increased in their hatred.

sections.title: VERSES 61-77 CHARACTERISTICS OF THE TRUE SERVANTS (BELIEVERS) OF ALLAH

arabic_lines: وَعِبَادُ الرَّحۡمٰنِ الَّذِيۡنَ يَمۡشُوۡنَ عَلَى الۡاَرۡضِ هَوۡنًا وَّاِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الۡجٰهِلُوۡنَ قَالُوۡا سَلٰمًا

translation.text: The ˹true˺ servants of the Most Compassionate are those who walk on the earth humbly, and when the foolish address them ˹improperly˺, they only respond with peace.

commentary.text: Attributes of the mature believer
(Read these Ayats with the hope that we can embody these characteristics)

The true servants of Allah SWT have a moderate walk that is calm, with a sense of dignity, humility and purpose not a walk that has arrogance and pride. And if the ignorant people insult them with bad words; they do not respond in kind, but forgive, overlook, and say nothing but good words such as Peace or the Salam of farewell, meaning they leave the place or situation.

translation.text: who pass their nights in prostrating themselves and standing before their Lord:

commentary.text: They spend a portion of the night in worship and in gratitude of all the blessings of the day. (Prostration is mentioned first because it is a position of humility.)
Note” Needless to say these people observe the five obligatory prayers.

translation.text: who pray, "Our Lord, save us from the torment of Hell, for its torment is killing:
it is an evil abode and an evil resting place":

commentary.text: They fear the torment of Hell and actively beg and plead for salvation.

translation.text: who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor miserly but keep the golden mean between the two (extremes):

commentary.text: They spend without excessiveness and are moderate in their spending. They are not stingy with their family and steer clear of spending on anything that is haram, such as, alcohol or anything that hints towards showing off. Thus, they spend and save.

translation.text: ˹They are˺ those who do not invoke any other god besides Allah, nor take a ˹human˺ life—made sacred by Allah—except with ˹legal˺ right, nor commit fornication. And whoever does ˹any of˺ this will face the penalty.

commentary.text: They do not commit major sins: (i) do not commit shirk (ii) nor kill/take innocent lives (except by just cause) (iii) Do not commit zina or adultery. FYI- The crime of zina and murder are interchangeable meaning they are both very serious offences and Iman leaves one’s soul after committing these offenses or crimes. There is a penalty/punishment for all these crimes.

translation.text: Their punishment will be multiplied on the Day of Judgment, and they will remain in it forever, in disgrace.

commentary.text: Punishment will be doubled meaning the physical torture of Hell will be coupled with the emotions of humiliation and disgrace. The crime of shirk, murder and zina are never isolated incidents as there are usually multiple sins committed prior to it. In addition, one will also carry the burden of those who follow your example and commit these sins.
Note: Some feel that here Allah SWT is talking about the punishment of the grave (Brazakh) which will happen before the DoJ.

translation.text: As for those who repent, believe, and do good deeds, they are the ones whose evil deeds Allah will change into good deeds. For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
In fact, the one who repents and does righteous deeds, returns to Allah as one rightly should.

commentary.text: Except those who sincerely repent (leave the sin and do not repeat the offence) and leave the sins (shirk, zina and murder) then believe and do good deeds then such people are not only forgiven but their sins are turned into good deeds. Such is the power of true repentance!
FYI – This is especially true for converts to Islam whose sins are erased and converted into good deeds. Born Again Muslim means the slate is as clean as the day he/she was born.
DEFINITION OF SUCCESS
Repent + Good deeds = Success

translation.text: (And the servants of the Merciful are those:) who do not bear witness to falsehood and who; if they have ever to pass by what is vain, pass by like dignified people:

commentary.text: It is a major sin to give false testimony. This can also mean they don’t want to be part of injustice/falsehood of any kind. Additionally, if they even pass by useless company or activities etc., (where people are backbiting, partying etc.) they make a dignified escape. This way they don’t get involved in any haram activity.

translation.text: who do not behave like the blind and the deaf, when the Revelations of their Lord are recited to them for admonition;

commentary.text: They are not blind and deaf meaning they do not tune out when the Ayat’s of the Quran are being recited. They observe and reflect about what has been revealed, thus, they are not deaf and blind towards the Quran or the signs of Allah SWT.

arabic_lines: وَالَّذِيۡنَ يَقُوۡلُوۡنَ رَبَّنَا هَبۡ لَـنَا مِنۡ اَزۡوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيّٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ اَعۡيُنٍ وَّاجۡعَلۡنَا لِلۡمُتَّقِيۡنَ اِمَامًا

translation.text: who pray, "Our Lord, bless us with wives and children, who may be the comfort of our eyes, and make us leaders of the righteous. "

commentary.text: This is a beautiful dua: Allah SWT pls give me joy and peace through my family. Let us all be on the same page regarding matters of deen so that there is no friction or conflict within the family unit. And let me be the best teacher/leader so that we all become the servants of Rehman.

translation.text: It is they who will be rewarded with ˹elevated˺ mansions ˹in Paradise˺ for their perseverance, and will be received with salutations and ˹greetings of˺ peace, staying there forever.
What an excellent place to settle and reside!

commentary.text: Such people will be rewarded with the best mansions in Paradise for their resolve, determination, steadfastness. They will be welcomed in Heaven with Salam and greetings of peace.

translation.text: O Muhammad, tell the people, "My Lord does not care at all if you do not invoke Him.
translation.ref_as_written: printed (25:76) a second time; this line and the following (25:77) line both quote 25:77, which the source split across two lines and mislabelled

translation.text: Now that you have denied (His Revelation), you will soon be awarded such a punishment which you will never be able to avoid."

commentary.text: The mushriqeen of Makkah are being addressed and thus so are we all: Allah SWT says: “You have denied! Now face the consequences.

items.text: For a believer the Quran defines our purpose in life, what our individual and collective rights/duties and responsibilities entail, what defines righteous or good deeds, what haram things we should avoid, etc etc.

(Name of Surah) Al-Furqan: The Criterion. The Quran has been called ‘Al-Furqan’ because it is the criterion for judging between right/halal and wrong/haram, virtue and vice, truth and falsehood. The Quran replaces confusion with clarity by providing answers so that we don’t decide for ourselves what is right and wrong. The Quran helps us understand and appreciate the majesty and might of our Raab and strengthens our faith by encouraging us to reflect upon the universe and think about the arguments and claims made by Allah SWT.

Thus, if a man is living life according to his own whims and desires – no matter how good/noble –then all his efforts will go to waste unless and until the actions/ deeds are performed for Allah SWT and in accordance to the prescribed manner of the sunnah.
Also see: (25:23) Then We will turn to whatever ˹good˺ deeds they did, reducing them to scattered dust.

The deeds of a disbeliever, no matter how good or noble, will be scattered like fine dust, thus, will hold no weight or value. This is because they were based on wrong beliefs that is, (i) they were not done exclusively for Allah SWT and (ii) not done according to the sunnah.
Lesson: Understand the criteria for what constitutes success in Islam so that one’s entire life efforts are not scattered like fine dust.
ESSENTIAL QUALITIES OF THE TRUE BELIEVER (The slave of Rehman)     عَعِبَادُ الرَّحۡمٰنِ
They walk the earth with dignity and humility and says 'Peace!' when the ignorant accost them. (Ayat 63)
They spend part of the night prostrating and standing in praise of their Raab. (Ayat 64)
They seek refuge from the torment of Hell. (Ayat 65)
They are moderate in their spending. (Ayat 67)
They do not commit shirk, commit murder, or zina. (Ayat 68)
They do not give false testimony and shun profanity and useless talk and company with dignity and grace. (Ayat 72)
When they are reminded of their Lord's revelations, attend with open ears and eyes. (Ayat 73)
They make dua: 'Our Lord, give us joy in our spouses and our children, and make us a model for those who fear You.  (Ayat 74)
These true Believers: "shall be rewarded for their fortitude with the loftiest places in Paradise. That is the best abode, and there they shall abide forever" (Ayat 75 and 76)

recaps.title: AGE OLD EXCUSES NOT TO BELIEVE

items.text: Why is the Messenger of Allah SWT a mere mortal? And why are angels not accompanying him or sent down as a Messenger?

(25:7) They say: "What sort of a Messenger is this: he eats food and walks about in the markets? Why was an angel not sent down to him so that he may remain with the Messenger and warn those that do not believe in him?

(25:21) Those who do not expect to meet Us say, “If only the angels were sent down to us, or we could see our Lord!” They have certainly been carried away by their arrogance and have entirely exceeded all limits.
Why should we obey and submit? Who is Rehman we only know Allah SWT?

(25:60) When they are told: "Prostrate yourselves before the Merciful One," they say: "What is the Merciful One? Shall we prostrate ourselves before whomsoever you command us to prostrate? This even further increases their aversion.
Why was the Quran revealed in stages and not all at once?

(25:32) Those who disbelieve say: "Why was the Quran not revealed to him all at once?" It was revealed thus that We may fully strengthen it upon your heart/mind; (and for the same end) We have revealed it gradually (according to a scheme) in fragments.
Following desires and making one’s whims one’s god/s.
(25:43) Have you ever considered the case of him who has taken his carnal desire for his god? Can you take responsibility for guiding him to the Right Way?

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text:
The Surah takes its name from Ayat 224 in which the word Ash-Shu`araa' occurs.
Note: This Surah should not be confused with Surah 42 -- Ash Shura (The Consultation).

items.text: وَالشُّعَرَآءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الۡغَاوٗنَؕ
(26:224) As for poets, only the wayward (defiant or errant) follow them.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Makkai Surah revealed about 6-7 years before the Hijrah.  It has 227 Ayats in 11 Rukus. Longest Makki Surah with short and rhythmic Ayats.

front_matter.label: Subject Matter and Topics
front_matter.text:
The background of this Surah is that the disbelievers of Makkah were persistently refusing (on one pretext or the other) to accept the message of Islam conveyed by the Holy Prophet (PBUH). The non-believers asked for signs/miracles to prove that the Quran was the word of Allah SWT.  They mocked the Prophet and branded him as a poet and sorcerer. This state of affairs was causing great anguish and grief to the Holy Prophet.
Such were the conditions when this Surah was revealed. It begins with words of consolation from Allah SWT to the Holy Prophet, implying, "Why do you worry for their sake? If these people have not believed in you, it is not because they have not seen any sign but because they are obdurate.
After this introduction until Ayat 191, one and the same theme has been presented continuously which is that: ‘The whole earth abounds in signs so as can guide a seeker of Truth to Reality, but the stubborn and misguided people have never believed even after seeing the signs, whether these were (i) signs of the natural phenomena or (ii) miracles of the Prophets.’
The history of seven ancient tribes has been narrated, who persisted in disbelief just like the disbelievers of Makkah. In this connection, the following points have been stressed:
Signs are of two kinds:( a) Those which are spread throughout the earth and by observing them one can judge whether what the Prophets are presenting is the Truth or not (b) signs or miracles that were witnessed by Pharaoh and his people, the nation of Nuh's, Ad, Thamud, Lut and the people of Aiykah.
The mentality of the disbeliever has been the same throughout the ages; their arguments, objections and their excuses for not believing have been the same and their ultimate fate has also been that same. Likewise, Prophets in every age presented the same teachings, and their personal character and their reasoning were the same. They were all similarly blessed by the mercy of Allah Almighty.
The above pattern of behavior and conduct found in history should make us reflect so that we do not repeat history by making the same mistakes.
Lastly, the discussion has been summed up, saying "O disbelievers, if at all you want to see the Signs, why should you insist on seeing those horrible Signs that visited the doomed communities of the past? Why don't you read/appreciate/understand the Quran which is being presented in your own language? Why don't you see Muhammad (upon whom be Allah's peace and mercy) and his Companions?

sections.title: 1-10 DEDICATION OF PROPHET MUHAMMAD (PBUH) FOR THE GUIDANCE OF MANKIND

translation.text: These are the Ayats of the Clear Book.

commentary.text: Al-Kitab-ul-Mubin الۡكِتٰبِ الۡمُبِيۡنِ means that the Quran is, beyond any doubt, a divine Book. Its language, diction, themes, facts presented in it and the background of its revelations, all testify to the fact that this is indeed the Book of the Master of all Creation. In this sense, its every sentence is a sign and a miracle.

The disbelievers of Makkah demanded a miracle from the Prophet (PBUH) so as to be convinced that the message he gave was really from Allah SWT. In answer to that, it has been said that if someone really wanted a sign for believing then study the Ayat’s of this Book (Quran.)

Then, the disbelievers accused the Prophet (PBUH) of being a sorcerer. This charge has been refuted by saying that the Quran has nothing ambiguous or mysterious in it, there are no hidden meanings; rather it plainly and clearly puts forward all of its teachings thus this cannot be the creation of a poet or a sorcerer’s imagination. (ESSENCE OF THIS SURAH).

translation.text: (O Muhammad), you will perhaps grieve yourself to death because these people do not believe.

commentary.text: Here is described the extreme anguish, guilt and grief the Prophet (PBUH) experienced over the Makkan disbelievers’ moral degradation, and their opposition to his message of reform. Sometimes it seemed as if his grief and mental suffering, for their sake, would cause his death. Allah SWT consoles his messenger.

translation.text: If We willed, We could send down upon them a ˹compelling˺ sign from the heavens, leaving their necks bent in ˹utter˺ submission to it.

commentary.text: Allah SWT could send down a miracle such that all would be forced to submit humbly. Thus, Allah SWT could compel them to believe. But such is not the way or plan of Allah SWT. There is no compulsion in religion. This world is but a place of test. So choose wisely!

translation.text: Whatever new reminder comes to them from the Most Compassionate, they always turn away from it.
They will soon come to know the truth of that which they have been scoffing (mocking) at

commentary.text: Allah SWT warns those who mock and turn away from the Quran that soon His threat of the DoJ will come true.

translation.text: Do they not look at the earth, how We caused a variety of fine vegetation to grow from it (in abundance)?

commentary.text: The abundance/variety of vegetation is a sign of Allah SWT’s existence. Reflect on all of Allah SWT’s creations and you will not need any miracles to believe. The whole universe is a sign from Allah SWT.

The seeker of truth does not have to look far for a sign from Allah SWT for example, the genius of vegetation whether it be the variety, abundance, the harmony within nature that is required for it to grow and flourish. Only someone who is bent upon disbelief will conclude that all this is happening without the wisdom, knowledge, power and design of an All-Mighty, All-Powerful Creator.

Clearly multiple masters and gods could not achieve this perfect harmony and accord between the soil, the sun and the moon, animals and plant life etc. A person, unless he is prejudiced and biased, cannot help feeling convinced that these are the clear signs and proofs of the existence of One God, and there is no need for further miracles to convince him of the reality of Tauhid.

arabic_lines: اِنَّ فِىۡ ذٰ لِكَ لَاٰيَةً ؕ وَّمَا كَانَ اَكۡثَرُهُمۡ مُّؤۡمِنِيۡنَ

translation.text: Surely there is a Sign in this, but most of them would not believe.
Verily Your Lord is Infinitely Mighty, Most Compassionate.

commentary.text: The above two Ayats will be repeated throughout this Surah. The Quran is NOT poetry yet the style here is like a poem. The style and rhythm of this Surah is meant to defeat the poets.

Often Al-Aziz or All Mighty is followed by All Wise but here All Mighty is followed by All Compassionate bec although Allah SWT has the power and might to show any miracle at any time, meaning, he could very easily have the whole world submit but it is His mercy and compassion that He does not hasten to punish the wrong-doer, but gives them respite for years and centuries to allow time to think, understand and mend their ways, and Allah SWT is ever ready to forgive the sins of a lifetime if the sinner offers repentance but once.
This opening passage shapes our understanding of the rest of this Surah.

sections.title: 11-33 ASSIGNMENT OF MUSA AS A RASOOL AND HIS DIALOGUE WITH FIR'ON AND MIRACLES OF PROPHET MUSA

arabic_lines: وَاِذۡ نَادٰى رَبُّكَ مُوۡسٰۤى اَنِ ائۡتِ الۡقَوۡمَ الظّٰلِمِيۡنَۙ

translation.text: (Recount to them about the time) when Your Lord called Moses: "Go to the wrong-doing people,

commentary.text: Historical events are being recounted beginning with the story of Prophet Musa (PBUH) and Pharaoh. The manifest signs (miracles) shown by Musa (PBUH) to Pharaoh during a public challenge conclusively established that what was presented by Musa (PBUH) was not magic. Even the skillful magicians of Pharon bore witness to this fact. Yet, some stubbornly continued to deny.
Now how can you, O’ people of Quraysh, say that you will believe only when you are shown a perceptible miracle and a physical sign?

arabic_lines: قَالَ كَلَّا ۚ فَاذۡهَبَا بِاٰيٰتِنَآ اِنَّا مَعَكُمۡ مُّسۡتَمِعُوۡنَ

translation.text: Allah responded, “Certainly not! So go, both of you, with Our signs. We will be with you, listening.

commentary.text: Prophet Musa (PBUH) was feeling apprehensive about confronting Pharon for many reasons including the fact there was a pending murder charge for when Musa (PBUH) accidently killed someone.  But Allah SWT reassures his Prophet that he will not be alone at any point. Allah SWT says He will attentively be listening.

Lesson: Whenever we do anything for Allah SWT, we should be fearless because Allah SWT not only equips us with the necessary means (whether it be companions, knowledge etc.,) but also, He is by our side watching and listening. So have full faith (tawakul) in Allah SWT.

sections.title: 34-51 FIR'ON TOOK PROPHET MUSA'S MIRACLES AS MAGIC AND SUMMONED THE MAGICIANS TO COMPETE AND AFTER WITNESSING A MIRACLE, ALL THE MAGICIANS EMBRACED ISLAM

intro.text: Pharon, summoned his best magicians to compete against Musa (PBUH) in a public competition.

translation.text: So the magicians fell down, prostrating.

commentary.text: When the magicians saw the signs/miracles presented by Musa (PBUH) they could not help themselves and fell into prostration. They knew that what Musa (PBUH) presented was not magic!
*Miracles included Musa (PBUH)’s staff changing into a snake and his hand became a white, glowing hand.

translation.text: saying: "We (now) believe in the Lord of the Universe,

commentary.text: The magicians declared their belief in Allah SWT -- without fear of Pharon.

sections.title: 52-68 DELIVERANCE OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL AND THE DESTRUCTION OF FIR'ON AND HIS CHIEFS

intro.text: Musa (PBUH) stayed in Egypt for a long time and Pharon and his chiefs continued to deny due to their arrogance and stubbornness therefore nothing was left except punishment and vengeance. Allah SWT commanded Musa PBUH), to migrate with the Children of Israel out of Egypt by night.

The following morning there was nobody to be found in the Israelite quarters. Pharon, in his anger, mobilized his troops including decision-makers, influential figures, ministers, nobles, leaders and soldiers. They then set in pursuit of Musa (PBUH) and the people of BI.

translation.text: Then We revealed to Moses, (commanding him): "Strike the sea with your rod." Thereupon the sea split up, and then each became like the mass of a huge mount.

commentary.text: It appears that as soon as Prophet Musa (PBUH) struck the sea with his staff, it tore the sea asunder and the waters stood like two mighty, high mountains on either sides and remained in that condition till the Israelite caravans passed through safely.

translation.text: We also brought the other party close to the same spot,

commentary.text: Pharoh and his army followed and were now reaching close to the same spot in the middle of the sea.

translation.text: and We delivered Moses and his companions, all of them,
then We drowned the others.

commentary.text: Musa (PBUH) and his followers crossed the sea safely. While, Pharaoh and his army were drowned and destroyed.

arabic_lines: اِنَّ فِىۡ ذٰ لِكَ لَاٰيَةً ؕ وَّمَا كَانَ اَكۡثَرُهُمۡ مُّؤۡمِنِيۡنَ

translation.text: Surely there is a Sign in this, but most of them would not believe.

commentary.text: In this there is a sign! Most people saw the miracles but still denied the Truth. May Allah SWT make us NOT of such a majority.

translation.text: Verily Your Lord is Infinitely Mighty, Most Compassionate.

commentary.text: Also see Ayat 8 and 9

Lesson: Pharoh, his chiefs and followers due to their arrogance and pride continued to deny despite being shown clear miracles for years. Finally, when they came to their senses, it was too late because they had been overtaken by the wrath of Allah SWT and the sea waters covered them completely. It was on this occasion that Pharon cried out: ‘I have believed that there is no god but the real God in Whom the Children of Israel have believed and I am of those who surrender.’ (Surah Yunus, Ayat 90).

There is a sign in this for the believers as well. We should understand how Allah SWT enables/facilitates the Truth to ultimately prevail and falsehood to depart despite that fact that at times the forces to evil may appear to be dominant and unstoppable.
Lessons and etiquettes of debate:
*Pharon was reactive, angry deceitful and fearful.
*Musa (PBUH) was proactive, calm, honest and focused.
Despite Pharon’s character assassination, insults and threats of imprisonment, Musa (PBUH) remained calm and on message that is:
(i)  I am a messenger of Allah SWT and (ii) stop persecuting and release the people of Bani Israel.
Only when all else failed Musa (PBUH) decided to present his miracles. Thus, he kept in reserve his most prized gift.

sections.title: 69-104 STORY OF PROPHET IBRAHIM AND HIS ARGUMENTS AGAINST IDOL WORSHIPPING AND PRAYER OF PROPHET IBRAHIM FOR THIS LIFE AND THE LIFE HEREAFTER AND MUSHRIKIN AND THEIR GODS BOTH WILL BE TOPPLED INTO HELL

translation.text: And recount to them the story of Abraham
when he asked his father and his people: "What do you worship?"
They replied, “We worship idols, to which we are fully devoted.”
Or can they benefit or harm you?”
They answered: "No; but we found our forefathers doing so.

commentary.text: How the Close Friend of Allah, Ibrahim spoke out against Shirk

Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH)’s story narrates the conflict between shirk and Tauhid. Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) encourages his nation to think and not just blindly follow their forefathers in such a critical issue as Iman. He encouraged them to think about why they worshiped inanimate objects that can never harm nor benefit them. The Quran is al-Furqan (the criteria) it provides proofs and constantly urges us to think and use our minds. Islam does not encourage blind faith.

The Quran has repeated this portion of Prophet Ibrahim’s life for the reason that the Arabs in general and the Quraysh, in particular, regarded themselves as the followers of Ibrahim (PBUH) and professed his way and creed. Besides them, the Christians and the Jews also claimed that Ibrahim (PBUH) was their religious leader and guide.

That is why the Quran admonishes them over and over again that the creed brought by Ibrahim (PBUH) was Islam itself, which is now being presented by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and which the Quraysh are opposing vehemently.
Thus, Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) was neither a Jew nor a Christian because Judaism and Christianity appeared centuries after him.
DESCRIPTION OF ALLAH BY PROPHET IBRAHIM (PBUH)

translation.text: Who created me and Who guides me;

commentary.text: The first reason for man to worship Allah SWT exclusively is that no one else is deserving of this honor. Allah SWT created us and guides us.

translation.text: Who gives me food and drink
and Who, when I am ill, heals me

commentary.text: The second reason for the exclusive worship of Allah SWT is that Allah SWT did not leave man alone (after creating him) to seek support and help from others rather He has also taken the responsibility of guiding, protecting and fulfilling man’s needs.

translation.text: Who will cause me to die and then will again restore me to life
Who, I hope, will forgive me my sins on the Day of Judgement.

commentary.text: The third reason for worshiping none but Allah SWT is that man’s relation with his God is not merely confined to this worldly life, which will end at death, but extends to the Hereafter. Every human being will have to rise at the command of Allah SWT and appear in His court. Then Allah SWT alone will decide whether to punish or to forgive.

arabic_lines: رَبِّ هَبۡ لِىۡ حُكۡمًا وَّاَلۡحِقۡنِىۡ بِالصّٰلِحِيۡنَۙ

translation.text: (And then Ibrahim prayed): "My Lord, endow me with knowledge and wisdom and join me with the righteous,

arabic_lines: وَاجۡعَلْ لِّىۡ لِسَانَ صِدۡقٍ فِى الۡاٰخِرِيۡنَۙ

translation.text: Bless me with honourable mention among later generations.
and make me of those who will inherit the Garden of Bliss,

commentary.text: Dua of Ibrahim (PBUH). (26:83 – 26:85)

Allah SWT give me knowledge and the wisdom/ability to retain and implement this knowledge. Join me with righteous company so that I can attain similar habits/deeds of the righteous. And grant me good mention/reputation and genuine praise from people of the later generations. And make me of those who enter paradise.

translation.text: Forgive my father, for he is certainly one of the misguided.
And do not disgrace me on the Day all will be resurrected—
the Day when neither wealth nor children will be of any benefit.

commentary.text: Dua of Ibrahim (PBUH). (26:86 – 26:88) continued:

Allah SWT pls forgive my father. Do not humiliate me on the DoJ. A day when one’s wealth nor one’s children will be of any use or help. (In this world often our money and children are our greatest source of comfort and benefit).

arabic_lines: اِلَّا مَنۡ اَتَى اللّٰهَ بِقَلۡبٍ سَلِيۡمٍؕ

translation.text: but only he that brings to Allah a sound heart will (attain to success)."

commentary.text: Dua of Ibrahim (PBUH). (26:89) continued:

A Sound or pure heart or Kalb-e-Saleem means a heart that is on fitra or as close to its original state as possible. A heart that is not filled or occupied by the wrong things. A heart that is God-fearing, free of sin, jealousy, rebellion (as much as possible). Thus, the only thing that will help us on the Day of Judgment is one who comes with a pure and sound heart.
DEFINITION OF SUCCESS
Sound or pure heart or Kalb-e-Saleem
Lesson: Desires and doubts create disease of the heart. The cure for doubt is to acquire knowledge. Spiritual nourishment is very important for a pure and clean heart.
Always remember the etiquette of making dua: First remember and praise Allah SWT and only then make dua. Meaning first acknowledge who is your Raab and show gratitude then you can ask.

arabic_lines: اِن فِىۡ ذٰ لِكَ لَاٰيَةً ؕ وَّمَا كَانَ اَكۡثَرُهُمۡ مُّؤۡمِنِيۡنَ

translation.text: Surely there is a Sign in this, but most of them would not believe.

commentary.text: Do not be part of the majority who do not believe. There is no greater lesson to be learnt.

translation.text: Verily Your Lord is Immensely Mighty, Ever Compassionate.

commentary.text: Also see Ayat 8, 9, 67 and 68
Though the Quran does not mention the torment that descended on Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) nation, it has included them among the tormented tribes.

Lesson: The story of Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) illustrates how on the one hand the mushriks of Arabia, especially the Quraysh, claimed that they were the proud followers of Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH), but on the other hand, they were blindly/ignorantly following their forefathers in shirk (idol worship).

There can be no greater misfortune than that man should turn away from Allah SWT, the one Who controls his life in this world as well as in the Hereafter and instead should turn for help and support to those who are utterly powerless.

Dawah lessons: (i) Start dawah with your near and dear ones. (ii) Practice what you preach. (iii) Encourage people to think as to why they believe. (iv) Always be gentle, kind and non-judgmental. (v) Even if they refuse to believe pray for them as Ibrahim (PBUH) continued to pray for his father and nation.

sections.title: 105-122 STORY OF PROPHET NUH, HIS DIALOGUE WITH HIS PEOPLE, THEY DISBELIEVED AND AS A RESULT FACED DESTRUCTION

translation.text: The people of Nuh, too, called the messengers liars.
Recall when their brother Nuh said to them: "Do you have no fear?

commentary.text: Nuh's preaching to His People, and Their Response

Prophet Nuh (PBUH) was the first messenger and he gave dawah for 950 years. The message of ALL Prophets is the same that is to remind people of their purpose in life and to be Allah conscious at all times. (Taqwa)

translation.text: I am a trustworthy Messenger to you;
so fear Allah and obey me.

arabic_lines: وَمَاۤ اَسۡـئَلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ اَجۡرٍۚ اِنۡ اَجۡرِىَ اِلَّا عَلٰى رَبِّ الۡعٰلَمِيۡنَۚ

translation.text: I seek of you no reward for this: my reward is with none except the Lord of the Universe.

commentary.text: Same message of all the messengers: (i) I am a faithful, reliable, honest messenger from Allah SWT. I do not distort or bend the truth so as to make it more palatable. (ii) Fear your Raab (have taqwa) and obey me. (iii)  I want no compensation. My reward is only with Allah SWT.

translation.text: They answered: "Shall we accept you even though it is the meanest of people who follow you?"

commentary.text: This shows that those who believed in Prophet Nuh (PBUH) were mostly poor people, the ordinary workmen, and youth who enjoyed no position in society. As for the influential and rich people, they had become the Prophets bitter opponents.

One of the arguments the disbelievers advanced against Prophet Nuh (PBUH) was that if there been any substance in Nuh’s message, then the religious divines and wise people of the community would have accepted it, but the only people who follow Nuh (PBUH) are those who belong to the lowest stratum of society. How can the noble and high-ranking people join the company of the common folks?

Precisely the same argument was being given by the unbelieving Quraysh regarding the Prophet (PBUH) and his followers. They argued that Muhammad (PBUH) was being followed by the poor and weak of their society and as such, if a thing was accepted by them then it was rejected by the chiefs, as it was devoid of any worth and value. The disbelievers of Makkah even went further. They argued that if God had to appoint a Prophet, then He would have appointed a great chief and not a mere mortal like Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

translation.text: They threatened, “If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be stoned ˹to death˺.”

commentary.text: They threatened to stone Nuh (PBUH) to death if he did not stop preaching.

translation.text: Noah prayed, “My Lord! My people have truly rejected me.
So judge between me and them decisively, and save me and the believers with me.”

commentary.text: Prophet Nuh prayed to Allah SWT to judge and then decide.

translation.text: Thereafter We rescued him and those who were with him in the laden Ark

commentary.text: Laden ship: because the ship became loaded with the believers and the pairs of animals from every species. This is how Allah SWT rescued the believers.

translation.text: and drowned the rest.

commentary.text: All who refused to believe were drowned Including Prophet Nuh’s son.

arabic_lines: َن فِىۡ ذٰ لِكَ لَاٰيَةً ؕ وَّمَا كَانَ اَكۡثَرُهُمۡ مُّؤۡمِنِيۡنَ

translation.text: Surely there is a Sign in this, but most of them would not believe.
Verily Your Lord is Immensely Mighty, Ever Compassionate

commentary.text: Also see Ayat 8, 9, 67, 68, 103 and 104

Lesson: Prophet Nuh (PBUH) remained with his nation for a thousand years save fifty years and struggled continuously to give dawahh. He studied their collective behavior, generation after generation, and finally came to the conclusion that these people had no inclination to accept the truth, and their future generations too would not adopt the righteous attitude.

This society based the value and worth of individuals dependent upon their profession or status in society and not their taqwa or beliefs. Worldly status and achievements were given priority over spiritual growth and superiority.

sections.title: 123-140 STORY OF PROPHET HUD, HIS ADDRESS TO HIS PEOPLE, THEY DISBELIEVED AND AS A RESULT FACED DESTRUCTION

translation.text: The people of Ad, too, called the messengers liars.
Recall, when their brother Hud said to them: "Have you no fear?

commentary.text: Prophet Hud was sent to the people of Ad:
After the destruction of the people of Nuh (PBUH), the nation of Ad was given power and prominence in the world.
Physically they were robust and powerful people.
Well-known in the world for their great skill and art in erecting lofty buildings with tall columns, they had no parallel as a nation in the world.

Material progress and physical power made them arrogant and vain causing them to deviate from the right path and adopted an arrogant attitude in the land. They said: ‘Who is mightier than us in power?’ (Surah Ha Mim Sajdah, Ayat 15).
Their political power was in the hands of a few tyrants before whom none could dare raise his voice.

Although they did not disbelieve in the existence of Allah SWT yet they were involved in shirk. They said (to Hud), ‘Have you come to us (with the demand) that we should worship Allah alone and discard those whom our elders have been worshiping?’ (Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayat 70).

translation.text: I am a trustworthy Messenger to you.
So fear Allah and obey me.

arabic_lines: وَمَاۤ اَسۡـئَـلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ اَجۡرٍۚ اِنۡ اَجۡرِىَ اِلَّا عَلٰى رَبِّ الۡعٰلَمِيۡنَ ؕ

translation.text: I seek of you no reward for this; my reward is with none but the Lord of the Universe.

commentary.text: Also see 107, 108 and 109

Same message of all the messengers: (i) I am a faithful, reliable, honest messenger from Allah SWT. I do not distort or bend the truth so as to make it more palatable. (ii) Fear your Raab (have taqwa) and obey me. (iii)  I want no compensation. My reward is only with Allah SWT.

translation.text: What, you build a monument on every hill merely for fun
and erect huge palaces as though you will live forever,

commentary.text: The grand buildings your erect are merely to show off your wealth and power, whereas they have no use and purpose except that they stand as monuments to your grandeur and glory. In order to make them grand, beautiful and strong, you expend all your wealth, mental and physical abilities as if you were going to live forever and there was no purpose of life except seeking of comfort and pleasure and nothing beyond this worldly life which might deserve your attention.

translation.text: and when you strike you strike like cruel tyrants?

commentary.text: Allah SWT provided this nation with so many blessings but instead of being grateful they were arrogant and oppressive with zero mercy for the weak and no justice for the poor who are being oppressed tyrannically. None was safe from their barbarities.
Lesson: Remember Allah SWT often and be grateful esp. when you have an abundance of blessings because these blessings are also a test from God and can be taken away at any moment.

commentary.text: According to the Quran, the people of Ad were destroyed by a violent windstorm. When they saw it advancing towards their valleys, they rejoiced hoping that the dense clouds would bring rain, but in reality, it was Allah’s scourge.

The nation of Thamud gained power and glory after the destruction of the nation of Ad. Following in the footsteps of their predecessor the standards of living went on rising higher and higher and the standards of humanity continued to fall lower and lower.

On the one hand, they erected large edifices on the plains and sculpted beautiful houses out of the hills like those in the caves of Ellora and Ajanta in India, while on the other hand, they became addicted to idol-worship and the worst men became leaders and rulers.

Prophet Saleh (PBUH) was sent as a messenger to this nation but his message of truth only appealed to the those belonging to the lower social strata as the people of the upper classes refused to believe in him.

translation.text: Saleh said: "This is a she-camel. There is a day set for her to drink and there is a day set for you to drink.

commentary.text: (156) So do not harm her, or the punishment of a terrible day will befall you.

This was not a common she-camel because it was presented in response to the demand for a miracle.

The people of Thamud were instructed that one day the she-camel will drink water, all alone, at your wells and springs and then one day you and your animals will take water and this arrangement cannot be violated in any way.
However, the day that the she-camel drank water she drank a lot. And although they were warned not to harm the she-camel in any way they paid no heed to the warnings and killed her.

arabic_lines: اِنَّ فِىۡ ذٰ لِكَ لَاٰيَةً وَمَا كَانَ اَكۡثَرُهُمۡ مُّؤۡمِنِيۡنَ

When this time limit came to an end, a violent explosion occurred around dawn, followed by a massive earthquake, which destroyed the whole nation completely. In the morning their dead bodies lay scattered like dry pieces of bush and neither their castles nor their caves could protect them against this calamity.

Lesson: Despite Allah SWT showing them the clear miracle of the she-camel they denied. Excessive over-indulgence in worldly pleasures made them heedless and they denied the Prophet calling him bewitched and a mere mortal.

sections.title: 192-207 AL-QURAN IS REVEALED IN PLAIN ARABIC BY ALLAH THROUGH ANGEL GABRIEL, THOSE PEOPLE WHO DO NOT WANT TO BELIEVE WILL NOT BELIEVE

translation.text: Indeed this is a revelation from the Lord of the Universe

commentary.text: Towards the end of this Surah the same theme with which the Surah began, is resumed. For reference, see Ayat 1-9. This eloquent, coherent, rational and luminous Book is not the product of the whims of a man. It has not been written and compiled by Muhammad (PBUH) himself rather is revelation from the Lord of this universe.

translation.text: (a revelation) in clear Arabic language,

commentary.text: The divine message has not been sent down in a dead or mysterious language, or in a language of riddles and enigmas, but in clear and eloquent Arabic, which can be understood easily by every Arab and every non-Arab who has learned Arabic. FYI: The Arabs trademark or expertise was their language and not tall buildings etc.

translation.text: And it has indeed been ˹foretold˺ in the Scriptures of those before.

commentary.text: This can have two meanings:
The revelation of the Quran was predicted in the previous Scriptures.

This divine message and teachings were also contained in the former Scriptures also, i.e the Torah, the Injeel and others. The same message of submission to One God, the same belief in the Hereafter and the same invitation to follow the Prophets has been given in all those Books. All the Books sent down by God condemn shirk and invite people to accept the true and sound philosophy of life, which is based on the concept of man’s accountability before God, and demands that man should give up his independence in deference to divine commands brought and preached by the Prophets.
Thus, none of this is new!

translation.text: Was it not sufficient proof for the deniers that it has been recognized by the knowledgeable among the Children of Israel?

commentary.text: The knowledgeable people of Bani Israel knew about the Quran from the Torah. When Khadija (the wife of the Prophet (PBUH) took the Prophet (PBUH), after his first revelation, to a scholar of B.I he confirmed the Prophethood.
The scholars of the Jews/Christians can testify regarding the coming of the last Prophet.

translation.text: Thus have We caused this (Admonition) to penetrate the hearts of the culprits (like a hot rod).

commentary.text: For some the Quran brings peace of mind and heart and yet for the disbelievers it passes like a hot iron rod through the heart, putting them ill at ease. The disbelievers start looking for maneuvers and ploys to deny the Quran. Thus, despite seeing all the signs around them they will not believe.

sections.title: 208-220 AL-QURAN IS NOT BROUGHT DOWN BY SHAITANS, IT IS NEITHER IN THEIR INTEREST NOR IN THEIR POWER

translation.text: The satans did not bring down this (Clear Book),

commentary.text: In Ayat 192 and 193 it states that the Quran is from Allah SWT and a Book that is clear and easy to understand.
Now it is being very clearly stated that the Quran has not been brought down by satans/jinns as the unbelieving Quraysh were asserting.

The Quraysh did not know how or why the Quran was moving the hearts of some so profoundly and deeply. Since they could not stop the Quran from reaching the people, they resorted to counteract its effect and influence by creating doubts and suspicions. Therefore, in their desperation they charged that Muhammad (PBUH) was a sorcerer, who was being inspired by the satans/jinns and they considered this charge of theirs to be the most effective because it could neither be easily verified nor refuted.

sections.title: 221-227 SHAITANS DESCEND ON SLANDERING SINNERS, WHO LISTEN TO HEARSAY AND ARE LIARS

translation.text: O people, shall I tell you on whom it is that satans descend?

commentary.text: The disbelievers of Makkah say that the Quran is brought down by satan or jinns. Allah SWT asks, “Shall I tell you upon whom satan descends?”

commentary.text: Satan comes down on those who lie and sin constantly. Impure for the impure.

commentary.text: And satan also comes down on those who read fortunes or predict the future. FYI – It is a sin to go to palm readers and fortune tellers because only Allah SWT decides our future.

translation.text: As for poets, only the wayward follow them.

commentary.text: Now the final group is being mentioned. Another falsehood being spread by the disbelievers of Makkah was that the Prophet was a poet reciting poetry. Allah SWT tells us about the character of most poets as compared to his Prophet (PBUH).

Poets were the social and cultural elite of Makkan society. The philosophical influencers who helped shape people’s beliefs/views on issues such as life, death and afterlife etc., came from poets. Poets were also the entertainment industry.  This Ayat is about the fanbase of the poets.
This Ayat refers to the characteristics, habits and temperament of the people who follow, admire and pursue poets which is in direct contrast from those who respect and accompany Muhammad (PBUH).

translation.text: Do you not see that they wander about in every valley

commentary.text: The poets and their followers are being addressed here. Both, roam aimlessly meaning they fearlessly delve into any subject that illicit a positive response from the audience no matter how offensive or vile. Valley is mentioned because they are descending into danger. They happily humiliate and degrade themselves, having no fixed belief or philosophy, simply to entertain.

Every new impulse makes them take up a new theme regardless as to whether it has any truth in it or not. If they felt pleased with somebody, they would exaggerate his praises, and if they felt offended by him, they would condemn him and run him down to hell. That is why, one can find God-worship and atheism, materialism and spiritualism, morality and immorality, piety and filthiness, seriousness and jesting, eulogy and satire expressed side by side in the poetry of one and the same poet.

This is in complete contrast to the Prophets across generations who kept repeating the same message of Allah SWT with no deviation. This is because they are not lost and wandering aimlessly. They are on a Straight path and have Straight-forward/honest speech. The Quran’s message is consistent and unwavering and words are clear and precise. The objective is clearly defined.

translation.text: and say things which they do not act upon,

commentary.text: Generally, the characteristics of the poets are the opposite of the Prophet’s (PBUH) conduct and practice. Prophet (PBUH) said what he practiced and practiced what he said. The fact that there was complete conformity between his word and deed could not be denied by anybody.
This is in complete contrast with poets who contradict themselves all the time.
