Disbelievers doubt Allah's power of creation and Al-Quran clarifies those matters in which the Israelites differ and A sign from the signs of doomsday (67-82)
Do not deny Allah's revelations without gaining their comprehensive knowledge (83-86)
A scene from the scenes of Doomsday and Those who accept guidance do so to their own good and those who go astray do so to their own peril (87-93)

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the phrase wad-in-naml which occurs in Ayat 18, implying that it is a Surah in which the story of An-Naml (the Ant) has been related.

items.text: حَتّٰٓى اِذَاۤ اَتَوۡا عَلٰى وَادِ النَّمۡلِۙ قَالَتۡ نَمۡلَةٌ يّٰۤاَيُّهَا النَّمۡلُ ادۡخُلُوۡا مَسٰكِنَكُمۡۚ لَا يَحۡطِمَنَّكُمۡ سُلَيۡمٰنُ وَجُنُوۡدُهٗۙ وَهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُوۡنَ
(27:18) And when they came across a valley of ants, an ant warned, “O ants! Go quickly into your homes so Solomon and his armies do not crush you, unknowingly.”

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
This Surah is of the middle Makkan period. According to Ibn Abbas and Jabir bin Zaid, "First the Surah Ash-Shu`araa' was sent down, then the Surah An Naml and then Al-Qasas."
This Surah has 93 Ayats in 7 Rukus.

front_matter.label: Subject and Topics
front_matter.text:
This Surah consists of two discourses, the first from the beginning of the Surah till Ayat 58, and the second from Ayat 59 till the end of the Surah.
THE THEME OF THE FIRST DISCOURSE is that only those people can benefit from the guidance of the Quran who accept, obey and submit.  One of the greatest hindrances for man regarding his belief/Iman is his denial of the Hereafter as it makes him reckless, selfish and given to this worldly life.
After this introduction three types of personalities have been presented:
The first group is characterized by Pharaoh, the chiefs of Thamud and the rebels of the nation of Lut, who were all heedless to any accountability of the Hereafter and had consequently become slaves to the world. These people did not believe even after seeing the miracles and persisted in their sinful ways They did not heed the admonition until just a moment before they were overtaken by the scourge of Allah SWT.
The second type of character is of the Prophet Solomon (PBUH), who had been blessed by God with unimaginable wealth, kingdom and grandeur. But, since he regarded himself as answerable before God and had the feeling that whatever he had was only due to Allah SWT's bounty, he adopted an attitude of obedience before Him and there was never even a hint of vanity in his character.
The third type is of the queen of Sheba who ruled over a most wealthy nation. Shirk was an ancestral way of life for her and her nation. But when the Truth became evident to her, nothing could stop her from accepting it. Her deviation was, in fact, due to her being born and brought up in a polytheistic environment and not because of her being a slave to her lusts and desires. Her conscience was not devoid of the sense of accountability before God.
IN THE SECOND DISCOURSE, attention has been drawn to some of the most glaring and visible realities of the universe, and the disbelievers of Makkah have been asked one question after the other to the effect : "Do these realities testify to the creed of shirk which you are following, or to the truth of Tawhid to which the Quran invites you?"
After this the real problem/issue of the disbelievers has been pointed out, saying, "The thing which has blinded them and made them insensitive to every glaring reality is their denial of the Hereafter that has rendered every matter and affair of life non-serious for the disbelievers. For, when according to them, everything has to become dust ultimately, then whole struggle of life is purposeless and without any objective, truth and falsehood are equal.

sections.title: 1-6 AL-QURAN IS A GUIDE AND GOOD NEWS TO THE BELIEVERS

arabic_lines: طٰسٓ تِلۡكَ اٰيٰتُ الۡقُرۡاٰنِ وَكِتَابٍ مُّبِيۡنٍۙ

translation.text: Ta'. Sin. These are the verses of the Quran and a Clear Book

commentary.text: Kitab-ul-Mubin  وَكِتَابٍ مُّبِيۡنٍۙا  means: (1) This Book presents its teaching, instructions and injunctions plainly and clearly (2) It distinguishes between the truth and falsehood and (3) It is a divine Book meaning that Allah SWT revealed it.

translation.text: ˹It is˺ a guide and good news for the believers:

commentary.text: The Ayat’s in the Quran provide clear and straight-forward guidance and convey good news but only for those who believe.

translation.text: who establish Prayer and give Zakah, and have firm faith in the Hereafter.

commentary.text: The Quran provides guidance and conveys good news of a good end but only to those who have Iman and then they practically follow Allah SWT laws and commandments by establishing regular prayer and pay zakat.

Although belief in the Hereafter is an article of faith, it has been mentioned separately here in order to stress its unique importance. That is, for those people who do not believe in the Hereafter, it is impossible to fully abide by the laws and commandments of the Quran because their criterion of good and evil is determined by worldly gain or loss. For a believer this world is but a place of test and the real life is yet to be experienced. Thus, all efforts and striving are for the Hereafter. Belief in the afterlife is a powerful motivator to stay the course.

translation.text: As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have made their deeds seem attractive to them so they stumble around in perplexity.

commentary.text: When man does not believe in life in the Hereafter and thinks that the outcome of his life’s struggle is confined to this world then he will inevitably develop a materialistic outlook on life, and the struggle between the truth and falsehood, morality and immorality etc., appears utterly meaningless. His real ambition will be to win successes and earn adornments in this worldly life without any moral qualms and inhibitions.

For such people the world, with all its glamor and pageantry, is made beautiful for them. Although their deeds are not actually good, they are deceived into thinking they are. Such people only live for today.

arabic_lines: اُولٰٓـئِكَ الَّذِيۡنَ لَهُمۡ سُوۡٓءُ الۡعَذَابِ وَهُمۡ فِى الۡاٰخِرَةِ هُمُ الۡاَخۡسَرُوۡنَ

translation.text: It is they who will suffer a dreadful torment, and in the Hereafter they will ˹truly˺ be the greatest losers.

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF THE GREATEST LOSERS

People whose entire efforts were only confined for this world and the entire time they deceived into thinking they were doing good or the right thing. Then indeed, for them is a painful and everlasting punishment and they are the “Greatest Losers.”

When they will go before their Lord, and all their deeds shall be placed in the scales, they will have no weight at all whether they had built great palaces, established great universities and libraries of which they were very proud in this world, will be worthless in the Hereafter.
The only deeds accepted by Allah SWT are those that are performed for Allah SWT and in accordance with the sunnah.
Also see Surah Kahf (103)
Say, (O Muhammad): "Shall We tell you who will be the greatest losers in respect of their works?
˹They are˺ those whose efforts are in vain in this worldly life, while they think they are doing good!”

It is they who reject the signs of their Lord and their meeting with Him, rendering their deeds void, so We will not give their deeds any weight on Judgment Day. That is their reward: Hell, for their disbelief and mockery of My signs and messengers.

Nothing definite has been said regarding the type, time or place of this “worst of punishment.” For some it is imposed in this world (in countless different ways); while others may experience it when they leave the world; some may experience it in the intermediary state between death and resurrection; and then after resurrection it will become endless and everlasting.

Lesson: Understand the worth of this world and act accordingly. Don’t get so engrossed in life, family, jobs etc., that you lose sight of the end game. Know the criteria for success i.e. Heaven and how to best achieve it.

sections.title: 7-14 STORY OF PROPHET MUSA'S SELECTION AS A RASOOL AND NINE SIGNS WERE SHOWN TO FIR'ON BUT HE STILL DISBELIEVED AND INCURRED ALLAH'S PUNISHMENT

intro.text: The Story of Musa and the End of Pharon

Here Allah SWT tells His Messenger Muhammad (PBUH) about what happened to Musa (PBUH), how Allah SWT chose him, spoke with him and gave him mighty signs with overwhelming proof and sent him to Pharon and his nation who denied the miracles/proof and arrogantly disbelieved.

arabic_lines: يٰمُوۡسٰۤى اِنَّـهٗۤ اَنَا اللّٰهُ الۡعَزِيۡزُ الۡحَكِيۡمُۙ

translation.text: O Moses, verily this is Me, Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise!
Now put your hand into your bosom, and it will come forth shining without any blemish. (These are two of the) nine Signs to be carried to Pharaoh and his people. They are surely a wicked people."

commentary.text: Prophet Musa (PBUH) had been granted nine clearly visible signs/miracles, which included: (1) Musa’s (PBUH) staff turning into a serpent, (2) his glowing/shining hand, (3) public triumph over the magicians, (4) occurrence of a widespread famine in the land as foretold by the Prophet Musa (5) the storm, (6) the locusts, (7) the incidence of weevils in the grain stores and of lice among human beings and animals, (8) the frogs, and (9) the rain of blood.

translation.text: But when Our Clear Signs came to them, they said: "This is plain magic."

commentary.text: These signs were plain and clear to see yet the Pharoh and his followers continued to denied.

translation.text: They denied those Signs out of iniquity and arrogance although their hearts were convinced of their truth. So see how evil was the end of those mischief-makers!

commentary.text: As mentioned at other places in the Quran, whenever a plague took place in Egypt, as foretold by the Prophet Musa (PBUH), the Pharaoh would say, “O Musa, pray to your Lord to remove this plague; then we shall submit to what you say.” But as soon as the plague was removed, the Pharaoh would break his promise.

The miracles presented by Prophet Musa were so manifest and clear that there was no room for doubt. Therefore, the real reason Pharaoh and his chiefs knowingly rejected Musa (PBUH) was due to their extreme pride, arrogance and their lust for powerful (which also made them extremely ruthless.)

The point of this story is to caution the people of Makkah: `O you who disbelieve in Muhammad and deny the Message that he has brought from his Lord, lest the same thing that befell them befall you also.'

sections.title: 15-19 STORY OF PROPHET SULEIMAN, TO WHOM ALLAH GAVE RULE OVER JINNS, MEN, BIRDS AND WINDS

translation.text: Indeed, We granted knowledge to David and Solomon. And they said ˹in acknowledgment˺, “All praise is for Allah Who has privileged us over many of His faithful servants.”

commentary.text: Dawud and Suleiman (peace be upon them), the organization of Suleiman's Troops and His passage through the Valley of the Ants

Here Allah SWT tells us about the blessings and favors which He bestowed upon two of His servants and Prophets, Dawud (David) and his son Suleiman (Solomon), peace be upon them both, and how they enjoyed power, authority and the position of being Prophets and Messengers.

At every moment where they could have should exhibited haughtiness and pride, they remained humble and grateful. The blessings that Allah SWT bestowed upon Suleiman included giving him complete authority and power, whereby mankind, the Jinn and the birds were subjugated to him. He also knew the language of the birds and animals, something that has never been given to any other human being -- as far as we know.

translation.text: Hosts of jinn and humans and birds were marshalled for Solomon and were kept under full control.

commentary.text: All of Suleiman's troops gathered together in a display of might and glory, with people marching behind him, followed by the Jinn, and the birds flying above his head.

translation.text: And when they came across a valley of ants, an ant warned, “O ants! Go quickly into your homes so Solomon and his armies do not crush you, unknowingly.”

commentary.text: When Prophet Suleiman (PBUH) and his army were passing through a valley which abounded in ants, he heard an ant calling out to the other ants, “Get into your holes, otherwise you will be trampled down by Suleiman's army without them even realizing.”

translation.text: So Solomon smiled in amusement at her words, and prayed, “My Lord! Inspire me to ˹always˺ be thankful for Your favours which You have blessed me and my parents with, and to do good deeds that please you. Admit me, by Your mercy, into ˹the company of˺ Your righteous servants.”

commentary.text: Suleiman (PBUH) was amazed and smiled at the ant’s speech and then made dua to Allah SWT, that ‘O my Raab! Inspire me to always be grateful and thankful for the wonderful powers and abilities that You have bestowed upon me lest I become a little forgetful or heedless with pride and go astray’.

A person having such a wonderful power of comprehension that he may hear and understand the speech of an ant is certainly something extraordinary and can involve a person in self-conceit and vanity. In such a case only the prayer of the Prophet Suleiman (PBUH) is relevant.
This was a very special quality of Suleiman (PBUH) that upon receiving any blessing or favor from Allah SWT he would immediately turn to Allah SWT in gratitude and humility.

Suleiman (PBUH) even as a young man recognizes his mortality and asks for entry into Paradise in the Hereafter that cannot come about merely on the strength of one’s good works, but is depent upon Allah’s mercy. According to a Hadith, the Prophet (PBUH) once said, “Merely the deeds of any one of you will not enable him to enter Paradise.” It was asked, “In your case too, O Messenger of Allah?” He replied, “Yes, I also shall not enter Paradise only on the strength of my deeds, unless Allah Almighty covers me with His mercy.”

sections.title: 20-31 THE HOOPOE BROUGHT HIM THE NEWS ABOUT THE QUEEN OF SHEBA AND LETTER FROM KING SULEIMAN TO THE QUEEN OF SHEBA

translation.text: I found there a woman ruling over them, one who has been endowed with all things and has a mighty throne.

commentary.text: When Suleiman (PBUH) took attendance of the birds the Hudhud was missing but soon came back and informed Suleiman (PBUH) about the people of Sheba where a woman was ruling a wealthy nation and she had an impressive throne.

translation.text: I found that she and her people prostrate themselves before the sun rather than Allah. Satan has made their deeds appear attractive to them and has, thus, debarred them from the Right Path so they do not find true guidance

commentary.text: This shows that the people of Sheba followed the religion of sun-worship. Satan made them believe that acquiring worldly wealth, with no regard to right or wrong, is the best use of their mental, intellectual and physical powers.

arabic_lines: اَللّٰهُ لَاۤ اِلٰهَ اِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ الۡعَرۡشِ الۡعَظِيۡمِ

translation.text: Allah - none is worthy of worship save He; He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.

commentary.text: (AYAT OF SAJDAH TALAWAT)

The object of performing a Sajdah here is that a believer should set himself apart from the sun-worshipers and should declare by his action that he does not regard the sun but Allah Almighty alone as his Deity and Lord.

sections.title: 32-37 COMMUNICATIONS BETWEEN QUEEN OF SHEBA AND SULEIMAN

arabic_lines: قَالَتۡ يٰۤاَيُّهَا الۡمَلَؤُا اِنِّىۡۤ اُلۡقِىَ اِلَىَّ كِتٰبٌ كَرِيۡمٌ

translation.text: The Queen said:" Know my nobles that a gracious letter has been delivered to me.

arabic_lines: اِنَّهٗ مِنۡ سُلَيۡمٰنَ وَاِنَّهٗ بِسۡمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحۡمٰنِ الرَّحِيۡمِۙ

translation.text: It is from Solomon, and it is: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."

commentary.text: It is proper etiquette to write بِسۡمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحۡمٰنِ الرَّحِيۡمِۙ  before any important document.

translation.text: (It says): "Do not act towards me with defiance, but come to me in submission."

commentary.text: The Queen suggested to her courtiers that the letter was important for several reasons: (1) It had reached her in an unusual way. Instead of an envoy it has been brought and dropped at her by a bird. (2) It was from Suleiman, the great ruler of Palestine and Syria. (3) It begins with the name of Allah, the Compassionate, and Merciful, which is an unusual way of correspondence and is not followed by any kingdom in the world (4) Then, it was also unusual that a letter should be written only in the name of Allah, the Exalted, (5) The most important thing in it was that it quite clearly and plainly invites us to give up rebellion and adopt obedience and present ourselves before Suleiman in submission (or as Muslims).

sections.title: 38-44 A MAN WHO HAD THE 'KNOWLEDGE OF THE BOOK' BROUGHT THRONE OF THE QUEEN TO KING SULEIMAN IN TWINKLING OF AND EYE AND QUEEN OF SHEBA AND HER PEOPLE EMBRACED ISLAM

translation.text: And he who had some knowledge of the Book said: "I will bring it before the twinkling of your eye." When Solomon saw the throne placed firmly beside him, he cried out: "This is by the grace of my Lord so that He may test me whether I give thanks for (His Bounty) or act with ingratitude. Whoever is grateful is so to his own good; and whoever is ungrateful, let him know that my Lord is Immensely Resourceful, Most Bountiful."

commentary.text: No explanation regarding the man was who had some knowledge of the Book has been given either in the Quran or in any authentic Hadith. Thus, this is from the Ayat Mutashabih.

Upon seeing the throne Prophet Suleiman (PBUH) exclaimed, “This is from the favor of my Lord..” and feared that the prompt arrangement of the throne might cause him to become ungrateful to Allah SWT instead of being grateful. Ingratitude only leads to the lessening of one’s blessings.

Lesson: Suleiman (PBUH) only showed gratitude and humility upon receiving blessings whether it was understanding the speech of the ants and now upon receiving the throne. There was never a sense of entitlement or pride as might be deemed natural for some.

translation.text: She was told: "Enter the palace." But when she saw it, she thought it was a pool of water and she bared both her calves (to enter into it). Solomon said: "This is a slippery floor of crystal. Thereupon she cried out: "My Lord, I have been inflicting much wrong on myself. Now I submit myself with Solomon to Allah, the Lord of the whole Universe."

commentary.text: It was said to the Queen to enter the palace. When she entered, she immediately lifted her garment (exposing her ankles) as she thought the smooth and flawless surface of glass or crystal was actually water.

The Queen realizes that Allah SWT has bestowed huge favors and blessings upon Suleiman (PBUH) and that Allah SWT can bestow what He wants on anyone He wishes. She understands that her throne or Suleiman (PBUH) kingdom is nothing compared to Allah SWT throne. She immediately submits.

Lesson: This is a brief account of the favors Allah SWT can bestow and how these favors continually increase a believer in his/her humility because they are not impressed with the worldly as much as they are with Allah SWT.

sections.title: 45-53 STORY OF PROPHET SALEH AND HIS ADDRESS TO HIS PEOPLE AND SALEH'S PEOPLE PLOTTED TO KILL HIM BUT ALLAH SAVED HIM AND DESTROYED THE DISBELIEVERS

translation.text: And We sent to Thamud their brother Saleh (with the Message): "Serve Allah," but all of a sudden they became split into two quarrelling factions.

commentary.text: One should note that precisely the same situation arose in Makkah at the advent of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). The nation became divided into two factions and a conflict started between them. Therefore, this story fully applies to the time and condition in which it was revealed.

translation.text: They said, ‘We see you and your followers as an evil omen.’ He replied, ‘God will decide on any omen you may see: you people are being put to the test.’

commentary.text: The chiefs considered Prophet Saleh cursed and blamed him for stirring up divisions in their nation, thus, turning brother against brother and separating son from father.

This very accusation was also being levelled against the Prophet (PBUH) by his opponents. Soon after he started his mission of inviting people to Islam, subsequently a delegation of the chiefs of the Quraysh went to Abu Talib to say, “Give up to us this nephew of yours: he has opposed your religion and your forefathers’ religion and has sown discord among your people, and has held the whole nation as foolish.”

A Prophet (any Prophet) comes to a nation as a test. Until Prophet Saleh’s arrival his nation did not recognize truth from falsehood; nor had any criterion for judging the genuine from the counterfeit. Now a criterion was brought against which all mankind will be judged and assessed. Thus, both truth and the falsehood have been made manifest.

Lesson: There is no such thing as a bad omen. All difficulty and all good takes place only with the permission and the decree of Allah SWT. When one is in a stressful situation instead of blaming it on others reflect upon your own actions and look within for answers.

translation.text: Now there were nine ring-leaders in the city who created corruption in the land and never worked to set things right.

commentary.text: There were nine chiefs of the tribes each of whom had a band of followers with him.

translation.text: They said: "Swear to one another in the name of Allah that we shall make a sudden night swoop on Saleh and his family and will then tell their heirs that we did not witness the destruction of his family. We are indeed truthful."

commentary.text: All the nine chiefs of Prophet Saleh’s (PBUH) tribe came together and swore to make a plan to execute Saleh in the middle of the night. This is so that no one tribe is held responsible whereby tribal warfare or a blood vengeance ensues.

The same was the situation in Makkah where the Quraysh were afraid that if they attacked and killed the Prophet (PBUH) then, Abu Talib, the chief of Bani Hashim, would come out with a claim to blood vengeance on behalf of his clan. This was precisely the kind of plot which the Makkan chiefs were devising against the Prophet (PBUH). Together all the clans would attack him so that the Bani Hashim could not hold any one clan responsible for the murder and therefore find it impossible to fight all of them the same time.

arabic_lines: وَمَكَرُوۡا مَكۡرًا وَّمَكَرۡنَا مَكۡرًا وَّهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُوۡنَ

translation.text: Thus they planned and We too planned, the while they did not know.

commentary.text: Before they could make the night attack on Prophet Saleh (PBUH), Allah SWT sent down His scourge which destroyed their nation completely.

Background: It appears that they made this plot after killing the she-camel. According to (Surah Hud: Ayat 65), when they had killed the she-camel, Prophet Saleh (PBUH) gave them three more days before they would be seized by the torment. At this they might have thought that the torment with which Saleh (PBUH) threatened them might come or might not, but they must take vengeance upon Saleh. Therefore, they probably chose the same night for the attack which Allah SWT had appointed for sending down the torment, and thus were struck down by Allah even before they could touch Prophet Saleh (PBUH).
Man proposes and God disposes. Always pray that Allah SWT is planning for you and not against you.

translation.text: So see what was the outcome of the plan they made: We utterly destroyed them and their people, all of them.
Now behold their houses that lie in utter ruins because of their wrong-doing. Verily there is a Sign in this for the people who know.

commentary.text: Some say that there is no link between Prophet Saleh (PBUH), the she-camel and the earthquake which struck the people of Thamud. These things have their natural causes and have nothing to do with the piety and wickedness of the people of a place. It is meaningless merely to say that such and such a city or land was filled with sin and wickedness, and therefore, it was overwhelmed by flood, or its habitation turned upside down by an earthquake, or it was ruined by a sudden disaster.

However, those who possess knowledge know that this universe is being ruled by an All-Wise, All-Knowing One Who is deciding destinies. His decisions to debase or exalt nations are not taken blindly but with wisdom and justice. In His Book of Law there is also included the principle of retribution, according to which the wicked are made to suffer for their evil deeds even in this world. The people who are aware of these realities, cannot explain away the occurrence of an earthquake by citing physical and natural causes; they will rather look upon them as the scourge of warning for themselves and they will learn lessons from it. They will try to understand those moral causes because of which the Creator annihilated a flourishing nation, which He Himself had created. They will divert their conduct and attitude from the track that brings Allah's wrath to the way that joins them to His mercy.

translation.text: And We delivered those who believed and who were faithful and mindful of Allah.

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF SUCCESS
Iman + Allah consciousness (taqwa) = Success

sections.title: 54-58 PROPHET LUT ADMONISHED HIS PEOPLE BUT THEY PAID NO HEED SO THEY FACED THE SCOURGE OF ALLAH

translation.text: We also sent Lot, and recall when he told his people: "Do you commit shameless acts with your eyes open?
Eventually We saved (Lot) and his family, except his wife. We had decreed that she should be among those who would remain behind.
And We rained down upon them a rain. It was an evil rain for those who had already been warned.

commentary.text: Now begins the story of Lut (PBUH) whose nation committed the most lewd and sinful acts of homosexuality in public. They too were destroyed and only those who believed were saved.

sections.title: 59- PRAISE TO ALLAH AND PEACE BE ON HIS RASOOLS

arabic_lines: قُلِ الۡحَمۡدُ لِلّٰهِ وَسَلٰمٌ عَلٰى عِبَادِهِ الَّذِيۡنَ اصۡطَفٰىؕ ءٰۤللّٰهُ خَيۡرٌ اَمَّا يُشۡرِكُوۡنَؕ

translation.text: Say, (O Muhammad):"All praise be to Allah, and peace be on those of His servants whom He has chosen." (Ask them): "Who is better: Allah or the false gods that they associate with Him as His partners?

commentary.text: From here starts the second discourse, and this is its introductory sentence. Superficially the question whether Allah SWT is better or the false deities appears to be odd. As a matter of fact, there can be no question of goodness in the false gods and, therefore, they cannot be compared to Allah. As for the polytheists, even they had no misconception that Allah SWT could be compared to their gods. But they were asked this question in order to be warned against their error.

After this, pointed questions have been asked, one after the other, about the manifestations of the power and creation of Allah to the effect: “Whose works are these? Is there besides Allah any other god also associated with these works? If not, why have you then set up these others as your deities?”
According to traditions, whenever the Prophet (PBUH) recited this verse, he would immediately respond to it, saying: “Nay, but Allah is better, and He alone is the Everlasting and Exalted and High.”
